subtitle: When the Peacock Throne Faced the Sword of Persia

panels.shot: split composition wide, half battlefield, half Delhi court, with both rulers facing each other across the divide
panels.action: On one side Nadir Shah stands in burnished mail on a dusty plain, horse rearing under him; on the other Muhammad Shah sits stiffly on a jeweled throne in a dim, fading hall, the two men locked in an invisible line of fate.

dialogue.text: In three hours at Karnal, Nadir Shah broke the Mughal army; in the weeks after, Delhi learned what a broken empire costs.

i18n.hi: कर्नाल के तीन घंटों में नादिर शाह ने मुग़ल फ़ौज तोड़ दी; बाद के हफ़्तों में दिल्ली ने टूटी सल्तनत की असली क़ीमत चुकाई।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high above the Indo-Iranian plateau, tracking east toward Hindustan
panels.action: Nadir Shah, gaunt and hawk-eyed, studies a map by lamplight in a Spartan tent, while far away Muhammad Shah lounges amid musicians and courtiers in a soft-lit palace, oblivious to the storm crossing the mountains.

dialogue.text: By the late 1730s, the Mughal sun still shone in Delhi, but its heat had gone. From Iran, a harder light approached—Nadir Shah, soldier-king of the Afsharids.

i18n.hi: 1730 के दशक के अंत तक दिल्ली में मुग़ल सूरज तो चमक रहा था, पर तपिश जा चुकी थी। ईरान से एक सख़्त रौशनी चली आ रही थी—अफ़्शारियों का सिपहसालार-बादशाह, नादिर शाह।

panels.shot: medium court-level shot in Delhi, slightly low angle on Muhammad Shah
panels.action: Muhammad Shah, richly robed yet tired in the eyes, sits at a darbar surrounded by ornate pillars and gossiping nobles, a petition in his hand ignored as nautch dancers twirl in the background.

dialogue.text: Muhammad Shah Rangila ruled a shrinking realm—its provinces slipping away, its nobles feuding, its armies brave but scattered and ill-led.

i18n.hi: मुहम्मद शाह रंगीला सिकुड़ती सल्तनत संभाल रहे थे—सूबे फिसल रहे थे, उमरा आपस में भिड़े थे, फ़ौजें बहादुर पर बिखरी और बे-सलाहियत थी।

panels.shot: dynamic battlefield planning shot in Nadir's camp, three-quarter view
panels.action: Nadir Shah bends over a rough sketch of the Indus and Ganga plains on the dirt, officers in plain armor around him, while a line of grim cavalry horses stands ready beyond the tent flap under cold dawn light.

dialogue.text: To the west, Nadir had forged Iran anew by sword and discipline. He saw in Hindustan not only wealth, but a chance to feed his army and bind his restless chiefs.

i18n.hi: पश्चिम में नादिर ने तलवार और अनुशासन से ईरान को फिर गढ़ा। उसे हिंदुस्तान में सिर्फ़ दौलत नहीं दिखी, बल्कि फ़ौज को खिलाने और अपने बेचैन सरदारों को बाँधने का मौक़ा भी।

panels.shot: wide panoramic shot of the plains near Karnal at sunrise
panels.action: Two vast camps face each other across the flat Karnal plain: on one side neat Afsharid lines with light artillery and camel-mounted guns, on the other a sprawling Mughal encampment of tents, elephants, and glittering but disorderly troops.

dialogue.text: On 24 February 1739, near Karnal, the two worlds met. Nadir’s hardened cavalry faced a Mughal host grand in show yet hollow in command.

i18n.hi: 24 फ़रवरी 1739 को, कर्नाल के पास, दो दुनिया आमने-सामने आ खड़ी हुईं। नादिर की सख़्त घुड़सवार फ़ौज के सामने एक ऐसी मुग़ल सेना थी जो दिखावे में शानदार, पर कमान में खोखली थी।

panels.shot: low-angle close shot on a Mughal war council tent
panels.action: Inside a richly carpeted Mughal command tent, Muhammad Shah listens as rival commanders gesture and argue, their hands on their sword-hilts, maps and orders scattered on a low table between them.

dialogue.speaker: nadir_shah_and_muhammad_shah
dialogue.text: “We have numbers and elephants. What can this Persian do?”

i18n.hi: “हमारे पास गिनती है, हाथी हैं। ये फ़ारसी हमारा क्या बिगाड़ लेगा?”

panels.shot: tight medium on Nadir Shah mounted, profile, with cavalry behind
panels.action: Nadir Shah sits straight in the saddle, face set and unreadable, as ranks of lean horsemen and camel-mounted zanburak guns stretch behind him in ordered lines, dust just beginning to rise.

dialogue.text: Nadir did not rush. His plan was simple and deadly—draw the Mughal chiefs out one by one into open ground, break them with fire and speed, then roll up what remained.

i18n.hi: नादिर ने हड़बड़ी नहीं की। उसकी चाल सीधी पर जानलेवा थी—मुग़ल सरदारों को एक-एक कर खुले मैदान में खींचो, आग और रफ़्तार से तोड़ो, फिर जो बचे उसे पीस दो।

panels.shot: wide action shot of the opening clash on the plains
panels.action: A Mughal division surges forward with elephants and cavalry in colorful armor, banners snapping, while ahead of them Afsharid cavalry feign retreat, light camel guns wheeling into position at their flanks.

dialogue.text: One Mughal wing advanced alone. Nadir’s horsemen fell back on purpose, luring them under the arcs of his camel-mounted zanburaks—small guns that spat iron into crowded ranks.

i18n.hi: एक मुग़ल बाज़ू अकेला बढ़ आया। नादिर के घुड़सवार जान-बूझ कर पीछे हटे, उन्हें ऊँटों पर रखे ज़नबूरकों की मार के नीचे खींच लाए—छोटी तोपें जो लोहे की बौछार से घनी क़तारें चीरती थीं।

panels.shot: medium, slightly overhead shot of Khan Dauran’s contingent in chaos
panels.action: In a swirl of dust and smoke, Mughal cavalry and elephants mill in confusion as Afsharid shots explode the ground around them; a distinguished Mughal commander figure slumps in his howdah, attendants reaching up in alarm.

dialogue.text: Under this fire, brave Khan Dauran pressed on and was mortally wounded. His fall shattered his men’s courage. The Mughal line bent where its loyalty had been strongest.

i18n.hi: इस आग में भी बहादुर ख़ान दौऱान आगे बढ़ते रहे और घातक ज़ख़्मी हुए। उनका गिरना ही उनकी क़तार का हौसला तोड़ गया। जहाँ वफ़ादारी सबसे मज़बूत थी, वहीं मुग़ल सफ़ टूटने लगी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Saadat Khan in the melee, then surrounded
panels.action: Saadat Khan’s richly armored figure leads a charge, face fierce, but in the next moment he and his retainers find themselves ringed by Afsharid horsemen, lances leveled, their circles tightening.

dialogue.text: Another pillar, Saadat Khan, rode into the storm and was taken alive. One after another, Mughal chiefs fought alone, without a single firm hand to knit their efforts.

i18n.hi: दूसरा सहारा, सआदत ख़ान, तूफ़ान में घुस पड़ा और क़ैद कर लिया गया। मुग़ल सरदार एक-एक कर अलग-अलग लड़े, और कोई मज़बूत हाथ उनकी कोशिशों को एक नहीं कर पाया।

panels.shot: wide aerial shot over the battlefield showing the rout
panels.action: From above, Afsharid squadrons sweep in arcs around broken Mughal clusters; elephants turn away from the fight, loose horses scatter, and a thick haze of dust hangs over the fleeing lines.

dialogue.text: Within about three hours, the Mughal army—once feared from Kabul to the Deccan—was in flight. Discipline and tactics had undone weight of numbers and splendor.

i18n.hi: करीब तीन घंटों में ही मुग़ल फ़ौज—जो कभी काबुल से दक्कन तक से डराई जाती थी—भंग हो कर भाग पड़ी। अनुशासन और चालबाज़ी ने संख्या और शान दोनों को मात दे दी।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot inside a Mughal command enclosure
panels.action: Muhammad Shah, pale and shaken, sits under a canopy with a handful of nobles; through the open side, distant Afsharid banners approach as a messenger kneels with captured standards laid at the emperor’s feet.

dialogue.speaker: nadir_shah_and_muhammad_shah
dialogue.text: “The field is lost, Padshah. Nadir demands your presence.”

i18n.hi: “मैदान हाथ से गया, बादशाह। नादिर आपकी हाज़िरी चाहता है।”

panels.shot: formal, symmetrical medium-wide shot of the two rulers meeting
panels.action: In a neutral pavilion between camps, Nadir Shah sits upright on a plain carpet, sword laid beside him, while Muhammad Shah stands hesitantly before him, jewels dim in the stark daylight, courtiers keeping a careful distance.

dialogue.text: The victor and the vanquished met in tented formality. Chronicles differ on every word spoken, but all agree that from Karnal onward, the Mughal emperor moved at Nadir’s will.

i18n.hi: फ़तहयाब और शिकस्त-ज़दा तम्बुओं में सजी रस्म में मिले। बयान हर लफ़्ज़ पर अलग हैं, पर सब मानते हैं कि कर्नाल के बाद से मुग़ल बादशाह नादिर की मर्ज़ी से चलने लगे।

panels.shot: wide tracking shot of the joint march towards Delhi
panels.action: A long column winds along the Grand Trunk Road: Nadir’s disciplined cavalry and camel guns, Mughal contingents marching subdued beside them, Muhammad Shah’s howdah in the midst, the domes of Delhi faint in the haze ahead.

dialogue.text: Nadir marched on Delhi with the Mughal ruler as his compelled guest. Some later writers praised, others condemned, the negotiations that followed—each reading motive into a record that speaks mainly of necessity.

i18n.hi: नादिर दिल्ली की ओर चला, मुग़ल बादशाह को मजबूर मेहमान बना कर साथ लिए। बाद की क़लमें कभी इन सौदों को सराहती, कभी कोसती हैं—हर एक अपने मतलब पढ़ती है, जबकि असल रिकार्ड ज़्यादातर मजबूरी की बात करता है।

panels.shot: wide, slightly elevated shot entering Delhi
panels.action: Nadir Shah rides through one of Delhi’s great gates, his troops filing in behind, while on the rooftops and lanes crowds press to see, some curious, some fearful, Mughal banners drooping beside Persian ones.

dialogue.text: Delhi, city of Shah Jahan’s dreams, saw foreign conquerors before. Yet now, for the first time since Babur, its own emperor entered as a shadow beside a stranger’s army.

i18n.hi: शाहजहाँ के ख़्वाबों की बस्ती, दिल्ली, ने पहले भी ग़ैर मुल्की फ़तहें देखी थीं। पर अब पहली बार बाबर के बाद ऐसा हुआ कि ख़ुद बादशाह किसी अजनबी की फ़ौज के साए में, बस परछाई बन कर शहर में दाख़िल हुआ।

panels.shot: interior wide shot of the Red Fort hall of audience
panels.action: Under the high arches of the Diwan-i-Khas, Muhammad Shah sits uneasily on the Peacock Throne, jewels glinting, while Nadir Shah stands nearby, expression coldly appraising, his guards lined along the marble walls.

dialogue.text: In the Diwan-i-Khas, the Peacock Throne still blazed with gems. Nadir saw in it not only beauty, but the treasure he needed to pay his men and secure his power at home.

i18n.hi: दीवान-ए-ख़ास में तख़्त-ए-ताऊस अब भी जवाहरात से दहक रहा था। नादिर ने उसमें सिर्फ़ ख़ूबसूरती नहीं, वो ख़ज़ाना देखा जो फ़ौज का हक़ अदा कर सके और घर की सल्तनत को मज़बूत करे।

panels.shot: street-level shot in a Delhi bazaar just before the riot
panels.action: A narrow lane in Delhi shows Afsharid soldiers moving in small groups, leading pack animals with loot, while townspeople watch with tightening faces, some whispering, some gripping concealed sticks and knives.

dialogue.text: Tension coiled in the city. Anand Ram Mukhlis, a Mughal courtier, later wrote how anger grew as Nadir’s men moved through markets and houses, taking what their king had promised them.

i18n.hi: शहर में तनाव सिमटता गया। मुग़ल दरबारी आनंद राम मुख़लिस ने बाद में लिखा कि कैसे ग़ुस्सा बढ़ता गया जब नादिर के सिपाही बाज़ारों और घरों में घूमते, वो सब उठा रहे थे जो उनके बादशाह ने उन्हें वादा किया था।

panels.shot: sudden, chaotic street-level shot of the crowd attack
panels.action: A Delhi crowd surges in a cramped lane, some attacking isolated Afsharid soldiers with sticks and daggers, an overturned cart blocking the path, while one fallen horse thrashes amid scattered bundles.

dialogue.text: Then came the spark—crowds attacked Nadir’s scattered soldiers. Sources from both sides agree: a riot, a clash, Afsharid dead in the lanes. What followed turned fury into catastrophe.

i18n.hi: फिर चिंगारी लगी—भीड़ ने बिखरे अफ़्शारी सिपाहियों पर धावा बोल दिया। दोनों तरफ़ के बयान मानते हैं: दंगा, भिड़ंत, गलियों में अफ़्शारी लाशें। जो आगे हुआ उसने ग़ुस्से को क़हर बना दिया।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot of Nadir Shah on a rooftop or raised platform
panels.action: On a flat rooftop, Nadir Shah stands rigid, sword unsheathed but lowered, looking over the city with a hard, distant gaze, plume stirring in the hot wind as smoke begins to rise from different quarters beyond.

dialogue.text: In the shock of that attack, Nadir ordered a general massacre. Anand Ram Mukhlis, near in time, speaks of around thirty thousand slain; Persian court accounts record fewer—each number a measure of a city’s trauma.

i18n.hi: उस हमले के सदमे में नादिर ने आम क़त्लेआम का हुक्म दिया। पास के गवाह आनंद राम मुख़लिस करीब तीस हज़ार क़त्ल का ज़िक्र करते हैं; फ़ारसी दरबारी किताबें इससे कम लिखती हैं—हर तादाद शहर के ज़ख़्म की एक माप है।

panels.shot: somber, wide street shot after the massacre has ceased
panels.action: A Delhi street lies eerily still at dusk, doors ajar, possessions abandoned, a few survivors moving like shadows; Afsharid sentries stand at cross-roads amid the emptiness, their faces unreadable.

dialogue.text: The killing stopped only when, as chronicles say, gold was promised and pleas were heard. Whether exaggeration or not, the silence that followed told its own story.

i18n.hi: क़त्ल तभी थमा जब, जैसा तवारीख़ कहती हैं, सोना देने का वादा हुआ और फ़रियादें सुनी गईं। बढ़ा-चढ़ा कर हो या नहीं, जो खामोशी उसके बाद छाई, वह अपना हाल खुद कह गई।

panels.shot: interior shot of treasure being inventoried and removed
panels.action: In a guarded chamber of the Red Fort, Afsharid officials and soldiers pack jewels, ingots, and ornaments into chests; behind them artisans disassemble the Peacock Throne, while Muhammad Shah watches from a distance, shoulders slumped.

dialogue.text: From Delhi’s vaults, Nadir took what he came for—immense treasure, the Peacock Throne, and famed gems like the Koh-i-Noor. Later tales embroidered their journeys; the sources are clearest only on their departure.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली के ख़ज़ानों से नादिर वही लेकर चला जिसके लिए आया था—बेशुमार दौलत, तख़्त-ए-ताऊस, और कोह-ए-नूर जैसे मशहूर हीरे। बाद की दास्तानों ने उनकी सफ़रनामे गढ़े; असली स्रोत उनके बस निकलने तक साफ़ हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Nadir’s departure from Delhi
panels.action: Outside the city walls, Nadir Shah rides at the head of a laden column of troops, animals straining under treasure, while on the ramparts Muhammed Shah stands small and distant, watching his conqueror depart with his empire’s wealth.

dialogue.text: When Nadir marched away, he left Muhammad Shah on the throne in name. But the spell was broken. Provincial powers saw how quickly the Mughal heartland had yielded to a single, sharp blow.

i18n.hi: जब नादिर फ़ौज ले कर लौटा, तो नाम भर को मुहम्मद शाह को तख़्त पर छोड़ गया। पर जादू टूट चुका था। सूबाई ताक़तों ने देख लिया कि मुग़ल दिल कितनी जल्दी एक तगड़ी, अकेली चोट से ढह सकता है।

panels.shot: closing medium shot, split composition of the two rulers in old age or reflection
panels.action: In a reflective split scene, an older Muhammad Shah sits alone in a dim chamber, head bowed over a rosary, while far away Nadir Shah, also aged, stares across a barren Iranian landscape, the weight of campaigns etched into both faces.

dialogue.text: Karnal and Delhi showed how an empire can stand bright yet hollow until one hard strike reveals the emptiness within; their echo asks every age where its own strength truly lies.

i18n.hi: कर्नाल और दिल्ली ने दिखा दिया कि सल्तनत ऊपर से दमकती रह सकती है, पर भीतर से खोखली हो; बस एक सख़्त वार ही भीतर की ख़ाली जगह उघाड़ देता है। उनकी गूँज हर ज़माने से पूछती है—तुम्हारी असली ताक़त आख़िर कहाँ है?

title_i18n.en: Karnal and the Three Hour Rout
title_i18n.hi: कर्नाल और तीन घंटे की हार
